instructions.task: Choose the next goal yourself from the observed cube. Use the strategy reference and recent work to decide whether to continue or change goal. strategyReference.objective: Solve every piece with its stickers matching the fixed centers. Yellow D first, white U last.
strategyReference.progression: A beginner route is daisy → yellow cross → yellow corners → middle edges → white cross → white corner orientation → corner placement → edge placement. Skip goals already achieved. Inspect prerequisites as well as the desired pattern: a white cross alone does not mean the lower layers are solved.
strategyReference.daisy: A daisy is a temporary scaffold: four yellow-up edges around the white U center. Build it when starting the yellow edges. Once complete, transfer its petals to the yellow D cross. During transfer the daisy shrinks intentionally: continue cross rather than rebuilding petals. If a yellow cross already exists, do not dismantle it to make a daisy.
strategyReference.preservation: Protect completed lower layers. A setup or partial operation can temporarily disturb a pattern; use previousGoal and recentActions to maintain a coherent plan. Change goal when its purpose is achieved or you decide the strategy needs repair. The previous goal is your earlier decision, not a command from code.
strategyReference.definitions: completed.topOriented describes white CORNERS only. completed.cornersPlaced checks corner locations, not sticker orientation. These facts are not recommended next actions. Choose orientation before permutation when needed. Finish by aligning the top with its side centers.

criteria.daisy: Put all four yellow edges around the white U center, with yellow stickers pointing U. These are petals. Preserve existing petals. Side colors do not need to match centers yet; already solved D edges may be moved to build the daisy. Use as the starting scaffold when the yellow cross is incomplete; not after a completed daisy is being transferred down.
criteria.cross: Solve the four yellow edges on D with side colors matching centers. You may use a daisy on U or insert directly. Use to transfer a complete daisy, continue its partial transfer, or pursue direct yellow-edge insertion. Skip when completed.cross=true.
criteria.first-layer: Solve yellow corners on D while preserving the yellow cross. Yellow cross must exist and yellow corners must still need work. Skip when completed.firstLayer=true.
criteria.middle-layer: Insert the four edges without white or yellow into the middle layer; preserve D. Choose when yellow bottom edges AND corners are solved but middle edges are not: firstLayer=true, middle=false.
criteria.top-cross: Orient white edge stickers toward U, preserving both lower layers. Both lower layers must be solved; white top edges still need orientation.
criteria.top-orientation: Orient all white corner stickers toward U, preserving the lower layers and top cross. Both lower layers and white top edges must be solved/oriented; white corners still need orientation.
criteria.top-corners: Position the oriented top corners in their correct destinations. Both lower layers and the white face must be complete; top corners still need placement or alignment.
criteria.top-edges: Permute the top edges and align U to finish. Lower layers and white orientation must be complete; finish edge permutation after corner placement, or final U alignment.

instructions.task: Choose the next goal yourself from the observed cube. Use the strategy reference and recent work to decide whether to continue or change goal. All goals are offered; none has been selected or recommended by the program. Do not choose a completed goal merely because its pattern looks familiar.

strategyReference.objective: Solve every piece with its stickers matching the fixed centers. Yellow D first, white U last.
strategyReference.progression: A beginner route is daisy → yellow cross → yellow corners → middle edges → white cross → white corner orientation → corner placement → edge placement. Skip goals already achieved. Inspect prerequisites as well as the desired pattern: a white cross alone does not mean the lower layers are solved.
strategyReference.daisy: A daisy is a temporary scaffold: four yellow-up edges around the white U center. Build it when starting the yellow edges. Once complete, transfer its petals to the yellow D cross. During transfer the daisy shrinks intentionally: continue cross rather than rebuilding petals. If a yellow cross already exists, do not dismantle it to make a daisy.
strategyReference.preservation: Protect completed lower layers. A setup or partial operation can temporarily disturb a pattern; use previousGoal and recentActions to maintain a coherent plan. Change goal when its purpose is achieved or you decide the strategy needs repair. The previous goal is your earlier decision, not a command from code.
strategyReference.definitions: completed.topOriented describes white CORNERS only. completed.cornersPlaced checks corner locations, not sticker orientation. These facts are not recommended next actions. Choose orientation before permutation when needed. Finish by aligning the top with its side centers.

criteria.daisy: Put all four yellow edges around the white U center, with yellow stickers pointing U. These are petals. Preserve existing petals. Side colors do not need to match centers yet; already solved D edges may be moved to build the daisy. Use as the starting scaffold when the yellow cross is incomplete; not after a completed daisy is being transferred down.
criteria.cross: Solve the four yellow edges on D with side colors matching centers. You may use a daisy on U or insert directly. Use to transfer a complete daisy, continue its partial transfer, or pursue direct yellow-edge insertion. Skip when completed.cross=true.
criteria.first-layer: Solve yellow corners on D while preserving the yellow cross. Yellow cross must exist and yellow corners must still need work. Skip when completed.firstLayer=true.
criteria.middle-layer: Insert the four edges without white or yellow into the middle layer; preserve D. Choose when yellow bottom edges AND corners are solved but middle edges are not: firstLayer=true, middle=false.
criteria.top-cross: Orient white edge stickers toward U, preserving both lower layers. Both lower layers must be solved; white top edges still need orientation.
criteria.top-orientation: Orient all white corner stickers toward U, preserving the lower layers and top cross. Both lower layers and white top edges must be solved/oriented; white corners still need orientation.
criteria.top-corners: Position the oriented top corners in their correct destinations. Both lower layers and the white face must be complete; top corners still need placement or alignment.
criteria.top-edges: Permute the top edges and align U to finish. Lower layers and white orientation must be complete; finish edge permutation after corner placement, or final U alignment.

strategyReference.objective: Solve every piece with its stickers matching the fixed centers. Yellow D first, white U last.
strategyReference.progression: A beginner route is daisy → yellow cross → yellow corners → middle edges → white cross → white corner orientation → corner placement → edge placement. Skip goals already achieved. Inspect prerequisites as well as the desired pattern: a white cross alone does not mean the lower layers are solved.
strategyReference.daisy: A daisy is a temporary scaffold: four yellow-up edges around the white U center. Build it when starting the yellow edges. Once complete, transfer its petals to the yellow D cross. During transfer the daisy shrinks intentionally: continue cross rather than rebuilding petals. If a yellow cross already exists, do not dismantle it to make a daisy.
strategyReference.preservation: Protect completed lower layers. A setup or partial operation can temporarily disturb a pattern; use previousGoal and recentActions to maintain a coherent plan. Change goal when its purpose is achieved or you decide the strategy needs repair. The previous goal is your earlier decision, not a command from code.
strategyReference.definitions: completed.topOriented describes white CORNERS only. completed.cornersPlaced checks corner locations, not sticker orientation. These facts are not recommended next actions. Choose orientation before permutation when needed. Finish by aligning the top with its side centers.

criteria.daisy: Put all four yellow edges around the white U center, with yellow stickers pointing U. These are petals. Preserve existing petals. Side colors do not need to match centers yet; already solved D edges may be moved to build the daisy. Use as the starting scaffold when the yellow cross is incomplete; not after a completed daisy is being transferred down.

criteria.middle-layer: Insert the four edges without white or yellow into the middle layer; preserve D. Choose when yellow bottom edges AND corners are solved but middle edges are not: firstLayer=true, middle=false.

criteria.top-orientation: Orient all white corner stickers toward U, preserving the lower layers and top cross. Both lower layers and white top edges must be solved/oriented; white corners still need orientation.
criteria.top-corners: Position the oriented top corners in their correct destinations. Both lower layers and the white face must be complete; top corners still need placement or alignment.
criteria.top-edges: Permute the top edges and align U to finish. Lower layers and white orientation must be complete; finish edge permutation after corner placement, or final U alignment.

instructions.task: Choose the next goal yourself from the observed cube. Use the strategy reference and recent work to decide whether to continue or change goal. All goals are offered; none has been selected or recommended by the program. Do not choose a completed goal merely because its pattern looks familiar.

strategyReference.objective: Solve every piece with its stickers matching the fixed centers. Yellow D first, white U last.
strategyReference.progression: A beginner route is daisy → yellow cross → yellow corners → middle edges → white cross → white corner orientation → corner placement → edge placement. Skip goals already achieved. Inspect prerequisites as well as the desired pattern: a white cross alone does not mean the lower layers are solved.
strategyReference.daisy: A daisy is a temporary scaffold: four yellow-up edges around the white U center. Build it when starting the yellow edges. Once complete, transfer its petals to the yellow D cross. During transfer the daisy shrinks intentionally: continue cross rather than rebuilding petals. If a yellow cross already exists, do not dismantle it to make a daisy.
strategyReference.preservation: Protect completed lower layers. A setup or partial operation can temporarily disturb a pattern; use previousGoal and recentActions to maintain a coherent plan. Change goal when its purpose is achieved or you decide the strategy needs repair. The previous goal is your earlier decision, not a command from code.
strategyReference.definitions: completed.topOriented describes white CORNERS only. completed.cornersPlaced checks corner locations, not sticker orientation. These facts are not recommended next actions. Choose orientation before permutation when needed. Finish by aligning the top with its side centers.

criteria.daisy: Put all four yellow edges around the white U center, with yellow stickers pointing U. These are petals. Preserve existing petals. Side colors do not need to match centers yet; already solved D edges may be moved to build the daisy. Use as the starting scaffold when the yellow cross is incomplete; not after a completed daisy is being transferred down.
criteria.cross: Solve the four yellow edges on D with side colors matching centers. You may use a daisy on U or insert directly. Use to transfer a complete daisy, continue its partial transfer, or pursue direct yellow-edge insertion. Skip when completed.cross=true.
criteria.first-layer: Solve yellow corners on D while preserving the yellow cross. Yellow cross must exist and yellow corners must still need work. Skip when completed.firstLayer=true.
criteria.middle-layer: Insert the four edges without white or yellow into the middle layer; preserve D. Choose when yellow bottom edges AND corners are solved but middle edges are not: firstLayer=true, middle=false.
criteria.top-cross: Orient white edge stickers toward U, preserving both lower layers. Both lower layers must be solved; white top edges still need orientation.
criteria.top-orientation: Orient all white corner stickers toward U, preserving the lower layers and top cross. Both lower layers and white top edges must be solved/oriented; white corners still need orientation.
criteria.top-corners: Position the oriented top corners in their correct destinations. Both lower layers and the white face must be complete; top corners still need placement or alignment.
criteria.top-edges: Permute the top edges and align U to finish. Lower layers and white orientation must be complete; finish edge permutation after corner placement, or final U alignment.

instructions.task: Choose the next goal yourself from the observed cube. Use the strategy reference and recent work to decide whether to continue or change goal. All goals are offered; none has been selected or recommended by the program. Do not choose a completed goal merely because its pattern looks familiar.

strategyReference.objective: Solve every piece with its stickers matching the fixed centers. Yellow D first, white U last.
strategyReference.progression: A beginner route is daisy → yellow cross → yellow corners → middle edges → white cross → white corner orientation → corner placement → edge placement. Skip goals already achieved. Inspect prerequisites as well as the desired pattern: a white cross alone does not mean the lower layers are solved.
strategyReference.daisy: A daisy is a temporary scaffold: four yellow-up edges around the white U center. Build it when starting the yellow edges. Once complete, transfer its petals to the yellow D cross. During transfer the daisy shrinks intentionally: continue cross rather than rebuilding petals. If a yellow cross already exists, do not dismantle it to make a daisy.
strategyReference.preservation: Protect completed lower layers. A setup or partial operation can temporarily disturb a pattern; use previousGoal and recentActions to maintain a coherent plan. Change goal when its purpose is achieved or you decide the strategy needs repair. The previous goal is your earlier decision, not a command from code.
strategyReference.definitions: completed.topOriented describes white CORNERS only. completed.cornersPlaced checks corner locations, not sticker orientation. These facts are not recommended next actions. Choose orientation before permutation when needed. Finish by aligning the top with its side centers.

criteria.daisy: Put all four yellow edges around the white U center, with yellow stickers pointing U. These are petals. Preserve existing petals. Side colors do not need to match centers yet; already solved D edges may be moved to build the daisy. Use as the starting scaffold when the yellow cross is incomplete; not after a completed daisy is being transferred down.
criteria.cross: Solve the four yellow edges on D with side colors matching centers. You may use a daisy on U or insert directly. Use to transfer a complete daisy, continue its partial transfer, or pursue direct yellow-edge insertion. Skip when completed.cross=true.
criteria.first-layer: Solve yellow corners on D while preserving the yellow cross. Yellow cross must exist and yellow corners must still need work. Skip when completed.firstLayer=true.
criteria.middle-layer: Insert the four edges without white or yellow into the middle layer; preserve D. Choose when yellow bottom edges AND corners are solved but middle edges are not: firstLayer=true, middle=false.
criteria.top-cross: Orient white edge stickers toward U, preserving both lower layers. Both lower layers must be solved; white top edges still need orientation.
criteria.top-orientation: Orient all white corner stickers toward U, preserving the lower layers and top cross. Both lower layers and white top edges must be solved/oriented; white corners still need orientation.
criteria.top-corners: Position the oriented top corners in their correct destinations. Both lower layers and the white face must be complete; top corners still need placement or alignment.
criteria.top-edges: Permute the top edges and align U to finish. Lower layers and white orientation must be complete; finish edge permutation after corner placement, or final U alignment.

strategyReference.daisy: A daisy is a temporary scaffold: four yellow-up edges around the white U center. Build it when starting the yellow edges. Once complete, transfer its petals to the yellow D cross. During transfer the daisy shrinks intentionally: continue cross rather than rebuilding petals. If a yellow cross already exists, do not dismantle it to make a daisy.
strategyReference.preservation: Protect completed lower layers. A setup or partial operation can temporarily disturb a pattern; use previousGoal and recentActions to maintain a coherent plan. Change goal when its purpose is achieved or you decide the strategy needs repair. The previous goal is your earlier decision, not a command from code.
strategyReference.definitions: completed.topOriented describes white CORNERS only. completed.cornersPlaced checks corner locations, not sticker orientation. These facts are not recommended next actions. Choose orientation before permutation when needed. Finish by aligning the top with its side centers.

criteria.daisy: Put all four yellow edges around the white U center, with yellow stickers pointing U. These are petals. Preserve existing petals. Side colors do not need to match centers yet; already solved D edges may be moved to build the daisy. Use as the starting scaffold when the yellow cross is incomplete; not after a completed daisy is being transferred down.
criteria.cross: Solve the four yellow edges on D with side colors matching centers. You may use a daisy on U or insert directly. Use to transfer a complete daisy, continue its partial transfer, or pursue direct yellow-edge insertion. Skip when completed.cross=true.
criteria.first-layer: Solve yellow corners on D while preserving the yellow cross. Yellow cross must exist and yellow corners must still need work. Skip when completed.firstLayer=true.
criteria.middle-layer: Insert the four edges without white or yellow into the middle layer; preserve D. Choose when yellow bottom edges AND corners are solved but middle edges are not: firstLayer=true, middle=false.
criteria.top-cross: Orient white edge stickers toward U, preserving both lower layers. Both lower layers must be solved; white top edges still need orientation.
criteria.top-orientation: Orient all white corner stickers toward U, preserving the lower layers and top cross. Both lower layers and white top edges must be solved/oriented; white corners still need orientation.
criteria.top-corners: Position the oriented top corners in their correct destinations. Both lower layers and the white face must be complete; top corners still need placement or alignment.
criteria.top-edges: Permute the top edges and align U to finish. Lower layers and white orientation must be complete; finish edge permutation after corner placement, or final U alignment.

definitions.cross: Bottom cross: D edge-center cells (row1 col2, row2 col1, row2 col3, row3 col2) equal D center, AND row3 col2 of EACH side F,R,B,L equals its own face center. Ignore D corners.
definitions.firstLayer: Bottom first layer: all nine D cells equal D center AND all three cells in row3 of EACH side F,R,B,L equal that side center. Ignore upper side rows and U.
definitions.lowerTwo: Lower two layers: bottom first layer as defined above is complete AND all three cells in row2 of EACH side F,R,B,L equal that side center. Ignore row1 of sides and U.
definitions.solved: Entire cube: every cell of each of the six faces equals that face center.

instructions.strategy: Use this beginner progression. If the cube is entirely solved, choose solved. Otherwise, if the lower two layers are complete, choose last-layer. Otherwise, if the first layer is complete, choose middle-layer. Otherwise, if the cross is complete, choose first-layer. Otherwise either daisy or cross is acceptable: daisy is a scaffold for the cross, while cross means direct cross construction. Never dismantle a complete cross to make a daisy. This experiment stops at the last-layer handoff; it does not choose among last-layer algorithms.

criteria.daisy: Build a temporary daisy for an incomplete bottom cross
criteria.cross: Build or finish the bottom cross directly
criteria.first-layer: Finish bottom corners while retaining the completed cross
criteria.middle-layer: Solve middle edges while retaining the completed first layer
criteria.last-layer: Work on the last layer while preserving the completed lower two layers
criteria.solved: The entire cube is solved; stop

frame.note: Fixed frame. Yellow D first; white U last. Clockwise is viewed directly at the turned face.

state.goal: Put all four yellow edges around the white U center, with yellow stickers pointing U. These are petals. Preserve existing petals. Side colors do not need to match centers yet; already solved D edges may be moved to build the daisy.

target.instructions: Choose one unfinished piece for the current goal. Keep working on previousTarget while its stage goal is incomplete, so setup/staging is followed by insertion/lifting. Change target when the previous one is complete, absent from this stage, or excluded by recovery. When choosing a new target, prefer an accessible piece. Do not choose pieces marked stage goal complete. A solved bottom edge is NOT a complete daisy petal. For top-layer stages select whole.

criteria.DF: DF at DF; destination undefined; stage goal incomplete.
criteria.DB: DB at DB; destination undefined; stage goal incomplete.

intent_DR.instructions: Choose the immediate intention for the exact record at `stagePieces[0]`. Read its position and stickers, not the position suggested by its permanent piece identifier. lift.instructions: Choose the lift/flip whose stated starting POSITION and yellow sticker DIRECTION match target. Ignore occupied landing slots for this question; a separate setup decision will clear them. Do not choose lift-bottom unless target is at DF with yellow pointing D.

criteria.lift-bottom: Target at DF with yellow pointing D: F2 lifts it to UF yellow-up. Before lifting, UF should not contain an existing yellow-up petal. Algorithm in selected reference: F2
criteria.lift-middle-right: Target at FR with yellow pointing F: R lifts it to UR yellow-up. Before lifting, UR should not contain an existing yellow-up petal. Algorithm in selected reference: R
criteria.lift-middle-left: Target at FL with yellow pointing F: L-prime lifts it to UL yellow-up. Before lifting, UL should not contain an existing yellow-up petal. Algorithm in selected reference: L'
criteria.stage-bottom-edge: Target at DF with yellow pointing F: F moves it to FL with yellow still pointing F. Requires UF free of yellow-up petals. This stages the edge in the middle, not yet a petal. On a later decision, clear UL and use lift-middle-left. Algorithm in selected reference: F
criteria.flip-top-edge: Target at UF with yellow pointing F: F then R lifts it via FR to UR yellow-up. Before executing, UR should not hold a yellow-up petal. Algorithm in selected reference: F R
criteria.lower-top-edge: Target at UF with yellow facing F, and the lift landing slots are occupied by petals: move it into FR first. Then a later U setup can clear UR before lifting it, without moving this target. Algorithm in selected reference: F
criteria.flip-top-edge-left: Target at UF with yellow pointing F: F-prime then L-prime lifts it via FL to UL yellow-up. UL must be clear of existing petals. Algorithm in selected reference: F' L'
criteria.reconsider: No described operation matches.

preparation.instructions: Decide whether preparation is needed before the selected lift. Inspect only the slots listed in mustBeFree. Unlisted slots do not matter. Every listed slot must be free of yellow-up petals. An empty mustBeFree list requires no preparation. Do not choose a rotation yet.

criteria.execute: Every required slot is free: execute the selected operation now.
criteria.clear: At least one required slot is occupied AND targetLayer is bottom or middle: clear space with a U turn, leaving the target stationary.
criteria.lower: At least one required slot is occupied AND targetLayer is top: lower the sideways edge to the middle first, so a later U turn can clear space without moving the target.

definitions.cross: Bottom cross: D edge-center cells (row1 col2, row2 col1, row2 col3, row3 col2) equal D center, AND row3 col2 of EACH side F,R,B,L equals its own face center. Ignore D corners.
definitions.firstLayer: Bottom first layer: all nine D cells equal D center AND all three cells in row3 of EACH side F,R,B,L equal that side center. Ignore upper side rows and U.
definitions.lowerTwo: Lower two layers: bottom first layer as defined above is complete AND all three cells in row2 of EACH side F,R,B,L equal that side center. Ignore row1 of sides and U.
definitions.solved: Entire cube: every cell of each of the six faces equals that face center.

instructions.strategy: Use this beginner progression. If the cube is entirely solved, choose solved. Otherwise, if the lower two layers are complete, choose last-layer. Otherwise either daisy or cross is acceptable: daisy is a scaffold for the cross, while cross means direct cross construction. Never dismantle a complete cross to make a daisy. definitions.cross: Bottom cross: D edge-center cells (row1 col2, row2 col1, row2 col3, row3 col2) equal D center, AND row3 col2 of EACH side F,R,B,L equals its own face center. Ignore D corners.
definitions.firstLayer: Bottom first layer: all nine D cells equal D center AND all three cells in row3 of EACH side F,R,B,L equal that side center. Ignore upper side rows and U.
definitions.lowerTwo: Lower two layers: bottom first layer as defined above is complete AND all three cells in row2 of EACH side F,R,B,L equal that side center. Ignore row1 of sides and U.
definitions.solved: Entire cube: every cell of each of the six faces equals that face center.

instructions.strategy: Use this beginner progression. If the cube is entirely solved, choose solved. Otherwise, if the lower two layers are complete, choose last-layer. Otherwise, if the first layer is complete, choose middle-layer. Otherwise, if the cross is complete, choose first-layer. Otherwise either daisy or cross is acceptable: daisy is a scaffold for the cross, while cross means direct cross construction. Never dismantle a complete cross to make a daisy. This experiment stops at the last-layer handoff; it does not choose among last-layer algorithms.
instructions.task: Choose the next goal. Use your previous assessments as the working progress description. They are model observations, not answers from a solver.

criteria.daisy: Build a temporary daisy for an incomplete bottom cross
criteria.cross: Build or finish the bottom cross directly
criteria.first-layer: Finish bottom corners while retaining the completed cross
criteria.middle-layer: Solve middle edges while retaining the completed first layer
criteria.last-layer: Work on the last layer while preserving the completed lower two layers
criteria.solved: The entire cube is solved; stop

frame.note: Fixed frame. Yellow D first; white U last. Clockwise is viewed directly at the turned face.

state.goal: Put all four yellow edges around the white U center, with yellow stickers pointing U. These are petals. Preserve existing petals. Side colors do not need to match centers yet; already solved D edges may be moved to build the daisy.

Do not choose pieces marked stage goal complete. A solved bottom edge is NOT a complete daisy petal. For top-layer stages select whole.

lift.instructions: Choose the lift/flip whose stated starting POSITION and yellow sticker DIRECTION match target. Ignore occupied landing slots for this question; a separate setup decision will clear them. Do not choose lift-bottom unless target is at DF with yellow pointing D.

criteria.lift-bottom: Target at DF with yellow pointing D: F2 lifts it to UF yellow-up. Before lifting, UF should not contain an existing yellow-up petal. Algorithm in selected reference: F2
criteria.lift-middle-right: Target at FR with yellow pointing F: R lifts it to UR yellow-up. Before lifting, UR should not contain an existing yellow-up petal. Algorithm in selected reference: R
criteria.lift-middle-left: Target at FL with yellow pointing F: L-prime lifts it to UL yellow-up. Before lifting, UL should not contain an existing yellow-up petal. Algorithm in selected reference: L'
criteria.stage-bottom-edge: Target at DF with yellow pointing F: F moves it to FL with yellow still pointing F. Requires UF free of yellow-up petals. This stages the edge in the middle, not yet a petal. On a later decision, clear UL and use lift-middle-left. Algorithm in selected reference: F
criteria.flip-top-edge: Target at UF with yellow pointing F: F then R lifts it via FR to UR yellow-up. Before executing, UR should not hold a yellow-up petal. Algorithm in selected reference: F R
criteria.lower-top-edge: Target at UF with yellow facing F, and the lift landing slots are occupied by petals: move it into FR first. Then a later U setup can clear UR before lifting it, without moving this target. Algorithm in selected reference: F
criteria.flip-top-edge-left: Target at UF with yellow pointing F: F-prime then L-prime lifts it via FL to UL yellow-up. UL must be clear of existing petals. Algorithm in selected reference: F' L'
criteria.reconsider: No described operation matches.

preparation.instructions: Decide whether preparation is needed before the selected lift. Inspect only the slots listed in mustBeFree. Unlisted slots do not matter. Every listed slot must be free of yellow-up petals. An empty mustBeFree list requires no preparation. Do not choose a rotation yet.

criteria.execute: Every required slot is free: execute the selected operation now.
criteria.clear: At least one required slot is occupied AND targetLayer is bottom or middle: clear space with a U turn, leaving the target stationary.
criteria.lower: At least one required slot is occupied AND targetLayer is top: lower the sideways edge to the middle first, so a later U turn can clear space without moving the target.

observations.frame: U top, D bottom, F front, B back, R right, L left. Every grid is viewed from outside. For F/R/B/L, row 3 touches D. For U the top of the grid touches B; for D the top touches F. Rows are top to bottom; columns left to right.

definitions.cross: Bottom cross: D edge-center cells (row1 col2, row2 col1, row2 col3, row3 col2) equal D center, AND row3 col2 of EACH side F,R,B,L equals its own face center. Ignore D corners.
definitions.firstLayer: Bottom first layer: all nine D cells equal D center AND all three cells in row3 of EACH side F,R,B,L equal that side center. Ignore upper side rows and U.
definitions.lowerTwo: Lower two layers: bottom first layer as defined above is complete AND all three cells in row2 of EACH side F,R,B,L equal that side center. Ignore row1 of sides and U.
definitions.solved: Entire cube: every cell of each of the six faces equals that face center.

instructions.strategy: Use this beginner progression. If the cube is entirely solved, choose solved. Otherwise, if the lower two layers are complete, choose last-layer. Otherwise, if the first layer is complete, choose middle-layer. Otherwise, if the cross is complete, choose first-layer. Otherwise either daisy or cross is acceptable: daisy is a scaffold for the cross, while cross means direct cross construction. Never dismantle a complete cross to make a daisy. This experiment stops at the last-layer handoff; it does not choose among last-layer algorithms.
instructions.task: Choose the next goal. Use your previous assessments as the working progress description. They are model observations, not answers from a solver.

criteria.daisy: Build a temporary daisy for an incomplete bottom cross
criteria.cross: Build or finish the bottom cross directly
criteria.first-layer: Finish bottom corners while retaining the completed cross
criteria.middle-layer: Solve middle edges while retaining the completed first layer
criteria.last-layer: Work on the last layer while preserving the completed lower two layers
criteria.solved: The entire cube is solved; stop

frame.note: Fixed frame. Yellow D first; white U last. Clockwise is viewed directly at the turned face.

state.goal: Solve yellow corners on D while preserving the yellow cross.

target.instructions: Choose one unfinished piece for the current goal. Keep working on previousTarget while its stage goal is incomplete, so setup/staging is followed by insertion/lifting. Change target when the previous one is complete, absent from this stage, or excluded by recovery. When choosing a new target, prefer an accessible piece. Do not choose pieces marked stage goal complete. A solved bottom edge is NOT a complete daisy petal. For top-layer stages select whole.

criteria.DRF: DRF at UFR; destination DRF; stage goal incomplete.
criteria.DBR: DBR at DRF; destination DBR; stage goal incomplete.
criteria.DFL: DFL at DFL; destination DFL; stage goal complete.
criteria.DLB: DLB at DLB; destination DLB; stage goal complete.

intent_DRF.instructions: Choose the immediate intention for the exact record at `stagePieces[0]`. Read its position and stickers, not the position suggested by its permanent piece identifier. Insertion staging positions: DRF→UFR, DFL→ULF, DLB→UBL, DBR→URB. ALIGN means only rotate U to place target directly above its destination. INSERT means use the short skill matching yellow sticker direction. EXTRACT means lift the misplaced bottom corner. REORIENT means use yellow-up insertion or a trigger. Preservation is required after a complete skill, not every internal turn.

criteria.align: Target is on top but not directly above its home bottom slot.
criteria.insert: Target is above its home bottom slot with yellow facing sideways.
criteria.reorient: Target is above its home with yellow pointing U.
criteria.extract: Target is in bottom but misplaced or twisted.

operation.instructions: Execute the chosenIntention, selecting just ONE next setup turn or complete skill. Insertion staging positions: DRF→UFR, DFL→ULF, DLB→UBL, DBR→URB. ALIGN means only rotate U to place target directly above its destination. INSERT means use the short skill matching yellow sticker direction. EXTRACT means lift the misplaced bottom corner. A setup need not solve the piece; insertion comes later.

criteria.right-trigger: Use when the target is at UFR with yellow facing U to reorient it, or at DRF misplaced/twisted to extract it. Does NOT insert a target at ULF, UBL, or URB: align it first. Algorithm in selected reference: R U R' U'
criteria.left-trigger: Use when the target is at ULF with yellow facing U to reorient it, or at DFL misplaced/twisted to extract it. Other U positions need alignment first. Algorithm in selected reference: L' U' L U
criteria.corner-insert: Insert target from UFR into DRF. Required: destination DRF, current position UFR, yellow sticker pointing R. If at another U corner, align it first. Algorithm in selected reference: R U R'
criteria.corner-insert-left: Insert target from ULF into DFL. Required: destination DFL, current position ULF, yellow sticker pointing L. If at another U corner, align it first. Algorithm in selected reference: L' U' L
criteria.corner-front-right: Insert target from UFR into DRF. Required: destination DRF, current position UFR, yellow sticker pointing F. Algorithm in selected reference: F' U' F
criteria.corner-front-left: Insert target from ULF into DFL. Required: destination DFL, current position ULF, yellow sticker pointing F. Algorithm in selected reference: F U F'
criteria.U: Turn U clockwise looking at that face. Only pieces touching U move. Their sticker directions change: F→L, L→B, B→R, R→F; the U sticker direction stays fixed. Corner positions: UFR→ULF, ULF→UBL, UBL→URB, URB→UFR. Edge positions: UF→UL, UL→UB, UB→UR, UR→UF.
criteria.U': Turn U counterclockwise looking at that face. Only pieces touching U move. Their sticker directions change: F→R, L→F, B→L, R→B; the U sticker direction stays fixed. Corner positions: UFR→URB, ULF→UFR, UBL→ULF, URB→UBL. Edge positions: UF→UR, UL→UF, UB→UL, UR→UB.
criteria.U2: Turn U 180 degrees looking at that face. Only pieces touching U move. Their sticker directions change: F→B, L→R, B→F, R→L; the U sticker direction stays fixed. Corner positions: UFR→UBL, ULF→URB, UBL→UFR, URB→ULF. Edge positions: UF→UB, UL→UR, UB→UF, UR→UL.
criteria.reconsider: No suitable action: stop for inspection rather than move arbitrarily.

definitions.cross: Bottom cross: D edge-center cells (row1 col2, row2 col1, row2 col3, row3 col2) equal D center, AND row3 col2 of EACH side F,R,B,L equals its own face center. Ignore D corners.
definitions.firstLayer: Bottom first layer: all nine D cells equal D center AND all three cells in row3 of EACH side F,R,B,L equal that side center. Ignore upper side rows and U.
definitions.lowerTwo: Lower two layers: bottom first layer as defined above is complete AND all three cells in row2 of EACH side F,R,B,L equal that side center. Ignore row1 of sides and U.
definitions.solved: Entire cube: every cell of each of the six faces equals that face center.

instructions.strategy: Use this beginner progression. If the cube is entirely solved, choose solved. Otherwise, if the lower two layers are complete, choose last-layer. Otherwise, if the first layer is complete, choose middle-layer. Otherwise, if the cross is complete, choose first-layer. Otherwise either daisy or cross is acceptable: daisy is a scaffold for the cross, while cross means direct cross construction. Never dismantle a complete cross to make a daisy. This experiment stops at the last-layer handoff; it does not choose among last-layer algorithms.

definitions.cross: Bottom cross: D edge-center cells (row1 col2, row2 col1, row2 col3, row3 col2) equal D center, AND row3 col2 of EACH side F,R,B,L equals its own face center. Ignore D corners.
definitions.firstLayer: Bottom first layer: all nine D cells equal D center AND all three cells in row3 of EACH side F,R,B,L equal that side center. Ignore upper side rows and U.
definitions.lowerTwo: Lower two layers: bottom first layer as defined above is complete AND all three cells in row2 of EACH side F,R,B,L equal that side center. Ignore row1 of sides and U.
definitions.solved: Entire cube: every cell of each of the six faces equals that face center.

instructions.strategy: Use this beginner progression. If the cube is entirely solved, choose solved. Otherwise, if the lower two layers are complete, choose last-layer. Otherwise, if the first layer is complete, choose middle-layer. Otherwise, if the cross is complete, choose first-layer. Otherwise either daisy or cross is acceptable: daisy is a scaffold for the cross, while cross means direct cross construction. Never dismantle a complete cross to make a daisy. This experiment stops at the last-layer handoff; it does not choose among last-layer algorithms.

criteria.cross: Build or finish the bottom cross directly

criteria.last-layer: Work on the last layer while preserving the completed lower two layers
criteria.solved: The entire cube is solved; stop

definitions.cross: Bottom cross: D edge-center cells (row1 col2, row2 col1, row2 col3, row3 col2) equal D center, AND row3 col2 of EACH side F,R,B,L equals its own face center. Ignore D corners.
definitions.firstLayer: Bottom first layer: all nine D cells equal D center AND all three cells in row3 of EACH side F,R,B,L equal that side center. Ignore upper side rows and U.
definitions.lowerTwo: Lower two layers: bottom first layer as defined above is complete AND all three cells in row2 of EACH side F,R,B,L equal that side center. Ignore row1 of sides and U.
definitions.solved: Entire cube: every cell of each of the six faces equals that face center.

instructions.strategy: Use this beginner progression. If the cube is entirely solved, choose solved. Otherwise, if the lower two layers are complete, choose last-layer. Otherwise, if the first layer is complete, choose middle-layer. Otherwise, if the cross is complete, choose first-layer. Otherwise either daisy or cross is acceptable: daisy is a scaffold for the cross, while cross means direct cross construction. Never dismantle a complete cross to make a daisy. This experiment stops at the last-layer handoff; it does not choose among last-layer algorithms.

frame.note: Fixed frame. Yellow D first; white U last. Clockwise is viewed directly at the turned face.

state.goal: Put all four yellow edges around the white U center, with yellow stickers pointing U. These are petals. Preserve existing petals. Side colors do not need to match centers yet; already solved D edges may be moved to build the daisy.

target.instructions: Choose one unfinished piece for the current goal. Keep working on previousTarget while its stage goal is incomplete, so setup/staging is followed by insertion/lifting. Change target when the previous one is complete, absent from this stage, or excluded by recovery. When choosing a new target, prefer an accessible piece. Do not choose pieces marked stage goal complete. A solved bottom edge is NOT a complete daisy petal. For top-layer stages select whole.

criteria.DR: DR at UR; destination undefined; stage goal complete.
criteria.DB: DB at UB; destination undefined; stage goal complete.

state.goal: Put all four yellow edges around the white U center, with yellow stickers pointing U. These are petals. Preserve existing petals. Side colors do not need to match centers yet; already solved D edges may be moved to build the daisy.

target.instructions: Choose one unfinished piece for the current goal. Keep working on previousTarget while its stage goal is incomplete, so setup/staging is followed by insertion/lifting. Do not choose pieces marked stage goal complete. A solved bottom edge is NOT a complete daisy petal. For top-layer stages select whole.

lift.instructions: Choose the lift/flip whose stated starting POSITION and yellow sticker DIRECTION match target. Ignore occupied landing slots for this question; a separate setup decision will clear them. Do not choose lift-bottom unless target is at DF with yellow pointing D.

criteria.lift-bottom: Target at DF with yellow pointing D: F2 lifts it to UF yellow-up. Before lifting, UF should not contain an existing yellow-up petal. Algorithm in selected reference: F2
criteria.lift-middle-right: Target at FR with yellow pointing F: R lifts it to UR yellow-up. Before lifting, UR should not contain an existing yellow-up petal. Algorithm in selected reference: R
criteria.lift-middle-left: Target at FL with yellow pointing F: L-prime lifts it to UL yellow-up. Before lifting, UL should not contain an existing yellow-up petal. Algorithm in selected reference: L'
criteria.stage-bottom-edge: Target at DF with yellow pointing F: F moves it to FL with yellow still pointing F. Requires UF free of yellow-up petals. This stages the edge in the middle, not yet a petal. On a later decision, clear UL and use lift-middle-left. Algorithm in selected reference: F
criteria.flip-top-edge: Target at UF with yellow pointing F: F then R lifts it via FR to UR yellow-up. Before executing, UR should not hold a yellow-up petal. Algorithm in selected reference: F R
criteria.lower-top-edge: Target at UF with yellow facing F, and the lift landing slots are occupied by petals: move it into FR first. Then a later U setup can clear UR before lifting it, without moving this target. Algorithm in selected reference: F
criteria.flip-top-edge-left: Target at UF with yellow pointing F: F-prime then L-prime lifts it via FL to UL yellow-up. UL must be clear of existing petals. Algorithm in selected reference: F' L'
criteria.reconsider: No described operation matches.

instructions.strategy: Use this beginner progression. If the cube is entirely solved, choose solved. Otherwise, if the lower two layers are complete, choose last-layer. strategyReference.objective: Solve every piece with its stickers matching the fixed centers. Yellow D first, white U last.
strategyReference.progression: A beginner route is daisy → yellow cross → yellow corners → middle edges → white cross → white corner orientation → corner placement → edge placement. Skip goals already achieved. Inspect prerequisites as well as the desired pattern: a white cross alone does not mean the lower layers are solved.
strategyReference.daisy: A daisy is a temporary scaffold: four yellow-up edges around the white U center. Build it when starting the yellow edges. Once complete, transfer its petals to the yellow D cross. During transfer the daisy shrinks intentionally: continue cross rather than rebuilding petals. If a yellow cross already exists, do not dismantle it to make a daisy.
strategyReference.preservation: Protect completed lower layers. A setup or partial operation can temporarily disturb a pattern; use previousGoal and recentActions to maintain a coherent plan. Change goal when its purpose is achieved or you decide the strategy needs repair. The previous goal is your earlier decision, not a command from code.
strategyReference.definitions: completed.topOriented describes white CORNERS only. completed.cornersPlaced checks corner locations, not sticker orientation. These facts are not recommended next actions. Choose orientation before permutation when needed. Finish by aligning the top with its side centers.

criteria.daisy: Put all four yellow edges around the white U center, with yellow stickers pointing U. These are petals. Preserve existing petals. Side colors do not need to match centers yet; already solved D edges may be moved to build the daisy. Use as the starting scaffold when the yellow cross is incomplete; not after a completed daisy is being transferred down.
criteria.cross: Solve the four yellow edges on D with side colors matching centers. You may use a daisy on U or insert directly. Use to transfer a complete daisy, continue its partial transfer, or pursue direct yellow-edge insertion. Skip when completed.cross=true.
criteria.first-layer: Solve yellow corners on D while preserving the yellow cross. Yellow cross must exist and yellow corners must still need work. Skip when completed.firstLayer=true.
criteria.middle-layer: Insert the four edges without white or yellow into the middle layer; preserve D. Choose when yellow bottom edges AND corners are solved but middle edges are not: firstLayer=true, middle=false.
criteria.top-cross: Orient white edge stickers toward U, preserving both lower layers. Both lower layers must be solved; white top edges still need orientation.
criteria.top-orientation: Orient all white corner stickers toward U, preserving the lower layers and top cross. Both lower layers and white top edges must be solved/oriented; white corners still need orientation.
criteria.top-corners: Position the oriented top corners in their correct destinations. Both lower layers and the white face must be complete; top corners still need placement or alignment.
criteria.top-edges: Permute the top edges and align U to finish. Lower layers and white orientation must be complete; finish edge permutation after corner placement, or final U alignment.

criteria.U: Turn U clockwise looking at that face. Only pieces touching U move. Their sticker directions change: F→L, L→B, B→R, R→F; the U sticker direction stays fixed. Corner positions: UFR→ULF, ULF→UBL, UBL→URB, URB→UFR. Edge positions: UF→UL, UL→UB, UB→UR, UR→UF.

criteria.U2: Turn U 180 degrees looking at that face. Only pieces touching U move. Their sticker directions change: F→B, L→R, B→F, R→L; the U sticker direction stays fixed. Corner positions: UFR→UBL, ULF→URB, UBL→UFR, URB→ULF. Edge positions: UF→UB, UL→UR, UB→UF, UR→UL.

layerMeasurements.note: Each count is out of four. firstLayer=true means ALL yellow edges AND yellow corners are already solved. middle=true means both lower layers are solved.

instructions.task: Choose the next goal yourself from the observed cube. Use the strategy reference and recent work to decide whether to continue or change goal. All goals are offered; none has been selected or recommended by the program. Do not choose a completed goal merely because its pattern looks familiar.

strategyReference.objective: Solve every piece with its stickers matching the fixed centers. Yellow D first, white U last.
strategyReference.progression: A beginner route is daisy → yellow cross → yellow corners → middle edges → white cross → white corner orientation → corner placement → edge placement. Skip goals already achieved. Inspect prerequisites as well as the desired pattern: a white cross alone does not mean the lower layers are solved.
strategyReference.daisy: A daisy is a temporary scaffold: four yellow-up edges around the white U center. Build it when starting the yellow edges. Once complete, transfer its petals to the yellow D cross. During transfer the daisy shrinks intentionally: continue cross rather than rebuilding petals. If a yellow cross already exists, do not dismantle it to make a daisy.
strategyReference.preservation: Protect completed lower layers. A setup or partial operation can temporarily disturb a pattern; use previousGoal and recentActions to maintain a coherent plan. Change goal when its purpose is achieved or you decide the strategy needs repair. The previous goal is your earlier decision, not a command from code.
strategyReference.definitions: completed.topOriented describes white CORNERS only. completed.cornersPlaced checks corner locations, not sticker orientation. These facts are not recommended next actions. Choose orientation before permutation when needed. Finish by aligning the top with its side centers.

criteria.daisy: Put all four yellow edges around the white U center, with yellow stickers pointing U. These are petals. Preserve existing petals. Side colors do not need to match centers yet; already solved D edges may be moved to build the daisy. Use as the starting scaffold when the yellow cross is incomplete; not after a completed daisy is being transferred down.
criteria.cross: Solve the four yellow edges on D with side colors matching centers. You may use a daisy on U or insert directly. Use to transfer a complete daisy, continue its partial transfer, or pursue direct yellow-edge insertion. Skip when completed.cross=true.
criteria.first-layer: Solve yellow corners on D while preserving the yellow cross. Yellow cross must exist and yellow corners must still need work. Skip when completed.firstLayer=true.
criteria.middle-layer: Insert the four edges without white or yellow into the middle layer; preserve D. Choose when yellow bottom edges AND corners are solved but middle edges are not: firstLayer=true, middle=false.
criteria.top-cross: Orient white edge stickers toward U, preserving both lower layers. Both lower layers must be solved; white top edges still need orientation.
criteria.top-orientation: Orient all white corner stickers toward U, preserving the lower layers and top cross. Both lower layers and white top edges must be solved/oriented; white corners still need orientation.
criteria.top-corners: Position the oriented top corners in their correct destinations. Both lower layers and the white face must be complete; top corners still need placement or alignment.
criteria.top-edges: Permute the top edges and align U to finish. Lower layers and white orientation must be complete; finish edge permutation after corner placement, or final U alignment.

state.goal: Solve yellow corners on D while preserving the yellow cross.

target.instructions: Choose one unfinished piece for the current goal. Keep working on previousTarget while its stage goal is incomplete, so setup/staging is followed by insertion/lifting. Change target when the previous one is complete, absent from this stage, or excluded by recovery. When choosing a new target, prefer an accessible piece. Do not choose pieces marked stage goal complete. A solved bottom edge is NOT a complete daisy petal. For top-layer stages select whole.

criteria.DRF: DRF at ULF; destination DRF; stage goal incomplete.
criteria.DFL: DFL at DFL; destination DFL; stage goal complete.
criteria.DLB: DLB at DLB; destination DLB; stage goal complete.
criteria.DBR: DBR at DBR; destination DBR; stage goal complete.

intent_DRF.instructions: Choose the immediate intention for the exact record at `stagePieces[0]`. Read its position and stickers, not the position suggested by its permanent piece identifier. Insertion staging positions: DRF→UFR, DFL→ULF, DLB→UBL, DBR→URB. ALIGN means only rotate U to place target directly above its destination. INSERT means use the short skill matching yellow sticker direction. EXTRACT means lift the misplaced bottom corner. REORIENT means use yellow-up insertion or a trigger. Preservation is required after a complete skill, not every internal turn.

criteria.align: Target is on top but not directly above its home bottom slot.
criteria.insert: Target is above its home bottom slot with yellow facing sideways.
criteria.reorient: Target is above its home with yellow pointing U.
criteria.extract: Target is in bottom but misplaced or twisted.

frame.note: All positions, sticker directions, and algorithm notation in this question use a reference with original F as F. U and D are unchanged. Piece IDs remain permanent identities.

state.goal: Solve yellow corners on D while preserving the yellow cross.

operation.instructions: Execute the chosenIntention, selecting just ONE next setup turn or complete skill. The target corner must move from target.position to the top slot directly above target.destination. DRF requires UFR; DFL requires ULF; DLB requires UBL; DBR requires URB. Use ONLY local destination, never original piece identity. Read U position cycles in the options. Avoid repeating an action from this exact state that already failed. A setup need not solve the piece; insertion comes later.

criteria.U: Turn U clockwise looking at that face. Only pieces touching U move. Their sticker directions change: F→L, L→B, B→R, R→F; the U sticker direction stays fixed. Corner positions: UFR→ULF, ULF→UBL, UBL→URB, URB→UFR. Edge positions: UF→UL, UL→UB, UB→UR, UR→UF.
criteria.U': Turn U counterclockwise looking at that face. Only pieces touching U move. Their sticker directions change: F→R, L→F, B→L, R→B; the U sticker direction stays fixed. Corner positions: UFR→URB, ULF→UFR, UBL→ULF, URB→UBL. Edge positions: UF→UR, UL→UF, UB→UL, UR→UB.
criteria.U2: Turn U 180 degrees looking at that face. Only pieces touching U move. Their sticker directions change: F→B, L→R, B→F, R→L; the U sticker direction stays fixed. Corner positions: UFR→UBL, ULF→URB, UBL→UFR, URB→ULF. Edge positions: UF→UB, UL→UR, UB→UF, UR→UL.
criteria.reconsider: No suitable action: stop for inspection rather than move arbitrarily.

instructions.task: Choose the next goal yourself from the observed cube. Use the strategy reference and recent work to decide whether to continue or change goal. All goals are offered; none has been selected or recommended by the program. Do not choose a completed goal merely because its pattern looks familiar.

strategyReference.objective: Solve every piece with its stickers matching the fixed centers. Yellow D first, white U last.
strategyReference.progression: A beginner route is daisy → yellow cross → yellow corners → middle edges → white cross → white corner orientation → corner placement → edge placement. Skip goals already achieved. Inspect prerequisites as well as the desired pattern: a white cross alone does not mean the lower layers are solved.
strategyReference.daisy: A daisy is a temporary scaffold: four yellow-up edges around the white U center. Build it when starting the yellow edges. Once complete, transfer its petals to the yellow D cross. During transfer the daisy shrinks intentionally: continue cross rather than rebuilding petals. If a yellow cross already exists, do not dismantle it to make a daisy.
strategyReference.preservation: Protect completed lower layers. A setup or partial operation can temporarily disturb a pattern; use previousGoal and recentActions to maintain a coherent plan. Change goal when its purpose is achieved or you decide the strategy needs repair. The previous goal is your earlier decision, not a command from code.
strategyReference.definitions: completed.topOriented describes white CORNERS only. completed.cornersPlaced checks corner locations, not sticker orientation. These facts are not recommended next actions. Choose orientation before permutation when needed. Finish by aligning the top with its side centers.

criteria.daisy: Put all four yellow edges around the white U center, with yellow stickers pointing U. These are petals. Preserve existing petals. Side colors do not need to match centers yet; already solved D edges may be moved to build the daisy. Use as the starting scaffold when the yellow cross is incomplete; not after a completed daisy is being transferred down.
criteria.cross: Solve the four yellow edges on D with side colors matching centers. You may use a daisy on U or insert directly. Use to transfer a complete daisy, continue its partial transfer, or pursue direct yellow-edge insertion. Skip when completed.cross=true.
criteria.first-layer: Solve yellow corners on D while preserving the yellow cross. Yellow cross must exist and yellow corners must still need work. Skip when completed.firstLayer=true.
criteria.middle-layer: Insert the four edges without white or yellow into the middle layer; preserve D. Choose when yellow bottom edges AND corners are solved but middle edges are not: firstLayer=true, middle=false.

criteria.top-orientation: Orient all white corner stickers toward U, preserving the lower layers and top cross. Both lower layers and white top edges must be solved/oriented; white corners still need orientation.
criteria.top-corners: Position the oriented top corners in their correct destinations. Both lower layers and the white face must be complete; top corners still need placement or alignment.
criteria.top-edges: Permute the top edges and align U to finish. Lower layers and white orientation must be complete; finish edge permutation after corner placement, or final U alignment.

strategyReference.objective: Solve every piece with its stickers matching the fixed centers. Yellow D first, white U last.
strategyReference.progression: A beginner route is daisy → yellow cross → yellow corners → middle edges → white cross → white corner orientation → corner placement → edge placement. Skip goals already achieved. Inspect prerequisites as well as the desired pattern: a white cross alone does not mean the lower layers are solved.
strategyReference.daisy: A daisy is a temporary scaffold: four yellow-up edges around the white U center. Build it when starting the yellow edges. Once complete, transfer its petals to the yellow D cross. During transfer the daisy shrinks intentionally: continue cross rather than rebuilding petals. If a yellow cross already exists, do not dismantle it to make a daisy.
strategyReference.preservation: Protect completed lower layers. A setup or partial operation can temporarily disturb a pattern; use previousGoal and recentActions to maintain a coherent plan. Change goal when its purpose is achieved or you decide the strategy needs repair. The previous goal is your earlier decision, not a command from code.
strategyReference.definitions: completed.topOriented describes white CORNERS only. completed.cornersPlaced checks corner locations, not sticker orientation. These facts are not recommended next actions. Choose orientation before permutation when needed. Finish by aligning the top with its side centers.

criteria.daisy: Put all four yellow edges around the white U center, with yellow stickers pointing U. These are petals. Preserve existing petals. Side colors do not need to match centers yet; already solved D edges may be moved to build the daisy. Use as the starting scaffold when the yellow cross is incomplete; not after a completed daisy is being transferred down.
criteria.cross: Solve the four yellow edges on D with side colors matching centers. You may use a daisy on U or insert directly. Use to transfer a complete daisy, continue its partial transfer, or pursue direct yellow-edge insertion. Skip when completed.cross=true.
criteria.first-layer: Solve yellow corners on D while preserving the yellow cross. Yellow cross must exist and yellow corners must still need work. Skip when completed.firstLayer=true.
criteria.middle-layer: Insert the four edges without white or yellow into the middle layer; preserve D. Choose when yellow bottom edges AND corners are solved but middle edges are not: firstLayer=true, middle=false.
criteria.top-cross: Orient white edge stickers toward U, preserving both lower layers. Both lower layers must be solved; white top edges still need orientation.
criteria.top-orientation: Orient all white corner stickers toward U, preserving the lower layers and top cross. Both lower layers and white top edges must be solved/oriented; white corners still need orientation.
criteria.top-corners: Position the oriented top corners in their correct destinations. Both lower layers and the white face must be complete; top corners still need placement or alignment.
criteria.top-edges: Permute the top edges and align U to finish. Lower layers and white orientation must be complete; finish edge permutation after corner placement, or final U alignment.

definitions.cross: Bottom cross: D edge-center cells (row1 col2, row2 col1, row2 col3, row3 col2) equal D center, AND row3 col2 of EACH side F,R,B,L equals its own face center. Ignore D corners.

instructions.strategy: Use this beginner progression. If the cube is entirely solved, choose solved. Otherwise, if the lower two layers are complete, choose last-layer. Otherwise, if the first layer is complete, choose middle-layer. Otherwise, if the cross is complete, choose first-layer. Otherwise either daisy or cross is acceptable: daisy is a scaffold for the cross, while cross means direct cross construction. Never dismantle a complete cross to make a daisy. This experiment stops at the last-layer handoff; it does not choose among last-layer algorithms.

criteria.cross: Build or finish the bottom cross directly

criteria.middle-layer: Solve middle edges while retaining the completed first layer
criteria.last-layer: Work on the last layer while preserving the completed lower two layers
criteria.solved: The entire cube is solved; stop

target.instructions: Choose one unfinished piece for the current goal. Keep working on previousTarget while its stage goal is incomplete, so setup/staging is followed by insertion/lifting. strategyReference.objective: Solve every piece with its stickers matching the fixed centers. Yellow D first, white U last.
strategyReference.progression: A beginner route is daisy → yellow cross → yellow corners → middle edges → white cross → white corner orientation → corner placement → edge placement. Skip goals already achieved. Inspect prerequisites as well as the desired pattern: a white cross alone does not mean the lower layers are solved.
strategyReference.daisy: A daisy is a temporary scaffold: four yellow-up edges around the white U center. Build it when starting the yellow edges. Once complete, transfer its petals to the yellow D cross. During transfer the daisy shrinks intentionally: continue cross rather than rebuilding petals. If a yellow cross already exists, do not dismantle it to make a daisy.
strategyReference.preservation: Protect completed lower layers. A setup or partial operation can temporarily disturb a pattern; use previousGoal and recentActions to maintain a coherent plan. Change goal when its purpose is achieved or you decide the strategy needs repair. The previous goal is your earlier decision, not a command from code.
strategyReference.definitions: completed.topOriented describes white CORNERS only. completed.cornersPlaced checks corner locations, not sticker orientation. These facts are not recommended next actions. Choose orientation before permutation when needed. Finish by aligning the top with its side centers.

criteria.daisy: Put all four yellow edges around the white U center, with yellow stickers pointing U. These are petals. Preserve existing petals. Side colors do not need to match centers yet; already solved D edges may be moved to build the daisy. Use as the starting scaffold when the yellow cross is incomplete; not after a completed daisy is being transferred down.
criteria.cross: Solve the four yellow edges on D with side colors matching centers. You may use a daisy on U or insert directly. Use to transfer a complete daisy, continue its partial transfer, or pursue direct yellow-edge insertion. Skip when completed.cross=true.
criteria.first-layer: Solve yellow corners on D while preserving the yellow cross. Yellow cross must exist and yellow corners must still need work. Skip when completed.firstLayer=true.
criteria.middle-layer: Insert the four edges without white or yellow into the middle layer; preserve D. Choose when yellow bottom edges AND corners are solved but middle edges are not: firstLayer=true, middle=false.
criteria.top-cross: Orient white edge stickers toward U, preserving both lower layers. Both lower layers must be solved; white top edges still need orientation.
criteria.top-orientation: Orient all white corner stickers toward U, preserving the lower layers and top cross. Both lower layers and white top edges must be solved/oriented; white corners still need orientation.
criteria.top-corners: Position the oriented top corners in their correct destinations. Both lower layers and the white face must be complete; top corners still need placement or alignment.
criteria.top-edges: Permute the top edges and align U to finish. Lower layers and white orientation must be complete; finish edge permutation after corner placement, or final U alignment.

operation.instructions: Execute the chosenIntention, selecting just ONE next setup turn or complete skill. ALIGN means rotate U until its side-facing color matches the center below it. INSERT from UF: upper sticker matching R goes right; upper sticker matching L goes left. EXTRACT uses an insertion to eject the wrong middle edge; preserve the completed bottom layer. criteria.middle-right: Insert UF into FR when its front sticker matches F and its upper sticker matches R. Can eject a wrong FR edge. Algorithm in selected reference: U R U' R' U' F' U F

criteria.U: Turn U clockwise looking at that face. Only pieces touching U move. Their sticker directions change: F→L, L→B, B→R, R→F; the U sticker direction stays fixed. Corner positions: UFR→ULF, ULF→UBL, UBL→URB, URB→UFR. Edge positions: UF→UL, UL→UB, UB→UR, UR→UF.
criteria.U': Turn U counterclockwise looking at that face. Only pieces touching U move. Their sticker directions change: F→R, L→F, B→L, R→B; the U sticker direction stays fixed. Corner positions: UFR→URB, ULF→UFR, UBL→ULF, URB→UBL. Edge positions: UF→UR, UL→UF, UB→UL, UR→UB.
criteria.U2: Turn U 180 degrees looking at that face. Only pieces touching U move. Their sticker directions change: F→B, L→R, B→F, R→L; the U sticker direction stays fixed. Corner positions: UFR→UBL, ULF→URB, UBL→UFR, URB→ULF. Edge positions: UF→UB, UL→UR, UB→UF, UR→UL.

decision.alg: U R U' R' U' F' U F

definitions.cross: Bottom cross: D edge-center cells (row1 col2, row2 col1, row2 col3, row3 col2) equal D center, AND row3 col2 of EACH side F,R,B,L equals its own face center. Ignore D corners.
definitions.firstLayer: Bottom first layer: all nine D cells equal D center AND all three cells in row3 of EACH side F,R,B,L equal that side center. Ignore upper side rows and U.
definitions.lowerTwo: Lower two layers: bottom first layer as defined above is complete AND all three cells in row2 of EACH side F,R,B,L equal that side center. Ignore row1 of sides and U.
definitions.solved: Entire cube: every cell of each of the six faces equals that face center.

instructions.strategy: Use this beginner progression. If the cube is entirely solved, choose solved. Otherwise, if the lower two layers are complete, choose last-layer. Otherwise, if the first layer is complete, choose middle-layer. Otherwise, if the cross is complete, choose first-layer. Otherwise either daisy or cross is acceptable: daisy is a scaffold for the cross, while cross means direct cross construction. Never dismantle a complete cross to make a daisy. This experiment stops at the last-layer handoff; it does not choose among last-layer algorithms.
instructions.task: Choose the next goal. Use your previous assessments as the working progress description. They are model observations, not answers from a solver.

criteria.daisy: Build a temporary daisy for an incomplete bottom cross
criteria.cross: Build or finish the bottom cross directly
criteria.first-layer: Finish bottom corners while retaining the completed cross
criteria.middle-layer: Solve middle edges while retaining the completed first layer
criteria.last-layer: Work on the last layer while preserving the completed lower two layers
criteria.solved: The entire cube is solved; stop

frame.note: Fixed frame. Yellow D first; white U last. Clockwise is viewed directly at the turned face.

state.goal: Insert the four edges without white or yellow into the middle layer; preserve D.

target.instructions: Choose one unfinished piece for the current goal. Keep working on previousTarget while its stage goal is incomplete, so setup/staging is followed by insertion/lifting. Change target when the previous one is complete, absent from this stage, or excluded by recovery. When choosing a new target, prefer an accessible piece. Do not choose pieces marked stage goal complete. A solved bottom edge is NOT a complete daisy petal. For top-layer stages select whole.

criteria.FR: FR at UF; destination FR; stage goal incomplete.
criteria.FL: FL at FL; destination FL; stage goal complete.
criteria.BR: BR at BR; destination BR; stage goal complete.
criteria.BL: BL at BL; destination BL; stage goal complete.

intention.instructions: Classify the chosen middle-layer edge. Trust solved: being in its destination SLOT is insufficient if flipped. If solved is true choose done. If solved is false and currentLayer is middle choose extract, even when it occupies its home slot. For an unsolved top edge choose insert if sideStickersMatchingCenters is nonempty, otherwise align.

criteria.extract: solved=false and currentLayer=middle
criteria.align: solved=false, currentLayer=top, sideStickersMatchingCenters is empty
criteria.insert: solved=false, currentLayer=top, sideStickersMatchingCenters is nonempty

reference.instructions: Compare referenceViews.F, referenceViews.R, referenceViews.B and referenceViews.L. Choose the view satisfying this reference requirement for the target. This renames coordinates, not a move. For a target on U, choose the reference whose front center equals target.sideFacingStickers[0].color. Do NOT match topStickerColor. For extraction, put its CURRENT middle position at FR. Do not choose front from its final destination for extraction.

observations.frame: U top, D bottom, F front, B back, R right, L left. Every grid is viewed from outside. For F/R/B/L, row 3 touches D. For U the top of the grid touches B; for D the top touches F. Rows are top to bottom; columns left to right.

definitions.cross: Bottom cross: D edge-center cells (row1 col2, row2 col1, row2 col3, row3 col2) equal D center, AND row3 col2 of EACH side F,R,B,L equals its own face center. Ignore D corners.
definitions.firstLayer: Bottom first layer: all nine D cells equal D center AND all three cells in row3 of EACH side F,R,B,L equal that side center. Ignore upper side rows and U.
definitions.lowerTwo: Lower two layers: bottom first layer as defined above is complete AND all three cells in row2 of EACH side F,R,B,L equal that side center. Ignore row1 of sides and U.
definitions.solved: Entire cube: every cell of each of the six faces equals that face center.

instructions.strategy: Use this beginner progression. If the cube is entirely solved, choose solved. Otherwise, if the lower two layers are complete, choose last-layer. Otherwise, if the first layer is complete, choose middle-layer. Otherwise, if the cross is complete, choose first-layer. Otherwise either daisy or cross is acceptable: daisy is a scaffold for the cross, while cross means direct cross construction. Never dismantle a complete cross to make a daisy. This experiment stops at the last-layer handoff; it does not choose among last-layer algorithms.

operation.instructions: Execute the chosenIntention, selecting just ONE next setup turn or complete skill. ALIGN means rotate U until its side-facing color matches the center below it. INSERT from UF: upper sticker matching R goes right; upper sticker matching L goes left. EXTRACT uses an insertion to eject the wrong middle edge; preserve the completed bottom layer. Avoid repeating an action from this exact state that already failed. A setup need not solve the piece; insertion comes later.

criteria.U: Turn U clockwise looking at that face. Only pieces touching U move. Their sticker directions change: F→L, L→B, B→R, R→F; the U sticker direction stays fixed. Corner positions: UFR→ULF, ULF→UBL, UBL→URB, URB→UFR. Edge positions: UF→UL, UL→UB, UB→UR, UR→UF.
criteria.U': Turn U counterclockwise looking at that face. Only pieces touching U move. Their sticker directions change: F→R, L→F, B→L, R→B; the U sticker direction stays fixed. Corner positions: UFR→URB, ULF→UFR, UBL→ULF, URB→UBL. Edge positions: UF→UR, UL→UF, UB→UL, UR→UB.
